The Real-World Challenge

Communication Shouldn't Have Barriers

People who communicate through sign language or gestures can face communication difficulties when interacting with people who do not understand those gestures. This can create barriers in education, healthcare, workplaces, public services and everyday interactions.

Communication Gap

The vast majority of the general public cannot understand sign language, leading to frequent misunderstandings and conversational isolation.

Limited Accessibility

Public service desks, health clinics, and educational hubs rarely have continuous assistive infrastructure for gesture-based communication.

Dependence on Intermediaries

Relying on specialized human interpreters is costly, not available 24/7, and restricts privacy in sensitive medical and legal settings.

Everyday Interaction Barriers

Simple day-to-day interactions—such as ordering food, asking for directions, or retail checkouts—become stressful bottlenecks.

Our Solution

Meet SignBridge

SignBridge uses computer vision and machine learning to recognize predefined hand gestures from a camera feed and convert them into readable text and speech.

Methodology & Logic

How SignBridge Works

A seamless seven-step computational pipeline converting raw camera photon signals into structured linguistic audio.

01

Camera Captures Hand

The webcam stream acquires real-time RGB video frames at standard web resolutions without requiring proprietary hardware or depth sensors.

02

MediaPipe Detects Hand

Google MediaPipe Hand Landmarker neural detector scans the frame to isolate palm boundaries and computes the region of interest.

03

21 Landmarks Extracted

Extracts high-precision 2.5D coordinates for 21 anatomical joints across wrist, thumb, index, middle, ring, and pinky fingers.

04

Normalization to 42 Features

Joint coordinates are translated relative to wrist landmark 0 and scaled by maximum joint distance, yielding 42 invariant numerical features.

05

Random Forest Classification

The pre-trained ensemble model evaluates decision trees on the 42 features to yield the predicted gesture class and confidence probability.

06

Conversion into Text

Validated classifications are parsed into readable transcriptions and appended to an interactive communication log for conversational clarity.

07

Speech Synthesis (Audio Out)

The synthesized text is vocalized via the browser's native Web Speech API with debounce filtering to prevent jarring repetition.

Engineering Stack

Built With Robust AI Technologies

A high-efficiency modular stack engineered for low latency, reproducible machine learning, and universal cross-device accessibility.

Language

Python 3.10+

Core programming language driving model training, data preprocessing, and API routing services.

Vision

OpenCV

Handles real-time camera frames, color conversion, image transformations, and bounding box computation.

Landmarks

MediaPipe

Detects and tracks 21 hand landmarks per frame with sub-pixel precision and high inference speed.

ML Toolkit

Scikit-learn

Provides the machine learning evaluation pipeline, hyperparameter tuning, and cross-validation tools.

Classifier

Random Forest

Classifies normalized hand landmark features into predefined gesture classes with high probabilistic stability.

Numerics

NumPy

Vectorized array operations for Euclidean distance calculations, wrist translation, and coordinate scaling.

Serialization

Joblib

High-speed model serialization and deserialization for loading signbridge_random_forest.pkl seamlessly.

Interface

Modern Web Client

Vanilla CSS & ES6+ JavaScript client with Web Speech API audio synthesis and Canvas landmark rendering.

Important Prototype Notice & Dataset Provenance

SignBridge currently recognizes a predefined set of hand gestures using a machine-learning model trained on the HaGRID (Hand Gesture Recognition Image Dataset). It does NOT claim to perform complete Indian Sign Language (ISL) translation. Rather, it serves as an AI accessibility proof-of-concept designed to be extended toward larger formal sign language vocabularies.

Transparency & Vision

Limitations & Future Roadmap

Honest engineering transparently acknowledges prototype boundaries while charting a clear evolutionary trajectory toward continuous sign language recognition.

CURRENT BOUNDARIES

Current Limitations

  • Predefined Gesture Vocabulary: Currently restricted to 19 discrete gesture classes trained from the HaGRID dataset.
  • One-Hand Recognition: Pipeline extracts landmarks for a single dominant hand, excluding two-handed compound signs.
  • Not Continuous Sign Language Translation: Does not parse syntactic sign language grammar, facial expressions, or complex sentence structures.
  • Environmental Dependencies: In extreme low-light environments or against busy cluttered backgrounds, landmark detection jitter can occur.
  • Generic Hand Gestures: Trained on standard computer-vision gesture datasets rather than a fully verified Indian Sign Language (ISL) corpus.
FUTURE ROADMAP

Future Expansion Roadmap

01
Larger Sign Language Vocabulary

Expanding the classifier to recognize hundreds of regional symbols.

02
Indian Sign Language (ISL) Datasets

Incorporating verified ISL corpora with regional dialect variations.

03
Two-Hand Gesture Recognition

Multi-hand landmarker tracking (42 landmarks) for compound signs.

04
Continuous Sentence Recognition

LSTM or Spatial-Temporal Graph Transformers for temporal motion.

05
Multilingual Speech Output

Real-time vocalization across Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and English.

06
Edge AI & Mobile Deployment

ONNX / TensorFlow Lite deployment for on-device smartphone inference.

Project Mission

Built as an AI Accessibility Project

SignBridge was developed to explore how lightweight computer vision models and machine learning pipelines can be combined to lower accessibility barriers. Rather than requiring bulky wearable data-gloves or cloud supercomputers, SignBridge proves that standard webcams and accessible algorithms can empower everyday assistive communication.
